newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soybean plants idle because of tax protest.
newsitem.headline: Indian soybean plants idle because of tax protest.

text.p: Production at soybean processing plants in central India have been at a standstill since May 1 because of protests over increased trade taxes, dealers said on Tuesday.
The processing industry in central India in a communication to its members barred plants and refineries from receiving or despatching any material until further notice.
The central state of Madhya Pradesh had doubled the mandi (market) tax to two percent and imposed other taxes from May 1.
Madhya Pradesh accounts for nearly 80 percent of the country's soybean production.
Traders said a delegation from the processing industry planned to meet state government officials to explain the industry's stand and seek the removal of the taxes.
They said no soymeal was available to buyers and exporters due to the strike.
Soymeal yellow was quoted at $330 per tonne free alongside ship compared with $262 at the same time last year.
